title: PR #27: Free shipping on orders of $50 or more

overview.whole_task: We're giving [[free-shipping-rule|free shipping on orders of $50 or more]], and the cart now tells shoppers how much more they need to add to get it.

footprint.label: Shop web app
footprint.change: A new free-shipping rule that the cart total and a new banner on the cart page both use.

ship_facts.deploy_order: Just a normal web app deploy.

overview.before_state: Every order paid a flat $5.99 for shipping, no matter how big it was.
overview.after_state: Orders of $50 or more ship free, and the cart shows how much more you need to add to get there.

visuals.caption: Here's the end result: a $62 cart gets [[free-shipping-banner|the green free-shipping banner]] and pays $0.00 for shipping.

concepts.what_it_is: The one place that decides shipping: $50.00 or more ships free, anything less pays $5.99.
how_it_works: **`shippingCost()`:** returns 0 for an empty cart or a subtotal of 5000 cents or more, and 599 otherwise.
**`amountLeftForFreeShipping()`:** returns how many cents are left to reach 5000, and never goes below 0.
concepts.pr_impact: New in this PR. The cart total and the banner both call it, so they can't disagree.

concepts.what_it_is: The cart keeps every price as a whole number of cents, like `priceCents` on each item.
how_it_works: **Why:** whole numbers add up exactly, while dollars with decimals can drift (0.1 + 0.2 isn't 0.3 in JavaScript).
**Display:** it only becomes text like $12.50 at the very end, through `formatMoney()`.
concepts.pr_impact: The new rule follows the same habit, so 5000 means $50.00.

concepts.what_it_is: The function that adds up the subtotal, shipping and total that the cart page shows.
how_it_works: **Subtotal:** price times quantity for every item in the cart.
concepts.pr_impact: Only its shipping line changes: it now asks the free-shipping rule instead of always using $5.99.

concepts.what_it_is: A one-line message at the top of the cart about free shipping.
how_it_works: **Under $50:** yellow, and says how much more to add.
**$50 or more:** green, and says you've got free shipping.
concepts.pr_impact: New in this PR, placed right under the "Your cart" heading.

chapters.title: The shipping rule
chapters.summary: One tiny file decides what shipping costs, with tests for the $50 line.

chapters.title: Using it in the cart
chapters.summary: [[cart-totals|The cart total]] switches to the new rule, and the cart page gets a banner.

steps.title: The [[free-shipping-rule|free-shipping rule]] in one small file
steps.explanation: First we put the whole rule in one place: $50 or more ships free, anything less pays $5.99.

rows: Add $12.50 more to get free shipping.
Add $0.01 more to get free shipping.

diff_highlights.title: All money is in cents
diff_highlights.explanation: Prices are [[money-in-cents|whole cents]] here, so 5000 means $50.00 and 599 means $5.99, which matches how the rest of the cart stores money and avoids rounding surprises.

diff_highlights.title: Empty cart, and exactly $50
diff_highlights.explanation: An empty cart still pays nothing, same as before, and the `>=` means a cart of exactly $50.00 already ships free.

diff_highlights.title: The $50 line is pinned by tests
diff_highlights.explanation: These two tests sit on either side of the line: $49.99 still pays $5.99, while exactly $50.00 ships free, so nobody can quietly turn `>=` into `>` later.

steps.title: The cart total uses the new rule
steps.explanation: Next we swap the old flat $5.99 in [[cart-totals|`cartTotals()`]] for the new rule, so the order summary follows it.

diff_highlights.title: The one-line swap
diff_highlights.explanation: The old line charged $5.99 whenever the cart had any items; now [[free-shipping-rule|`shippingCost()`]] decides from the subtotal and still returns $0 for an empty cart.

callouts.text: Heads up: this only changes the total the web app shows. Check that the payment server charges the same way, or a $60 order could show free shipping and still be charged $5.99.

steps.title: The "almost there" banner on the cart page
steps.explanation: Last, a [[free-shipping-banner|small banner at the top of the cart]] tells shoppers how close they are to free shipping.

points.text: The banner shows nothing at all.
It says how much more to add, using the same rule as the total.
It turns green and says you've got free shipping.

diff_highlights.title: Three cases, top to bottom
diff_highlights.explanation: Empty cart returns nothing, then if nothing is left to add we show the green message, and every other cart falls through to the "add $X more" text below.

visuals.label: Before
visuals.caption: Before: a $37.50 cart just pays $5.99, with no hint that free shipping exists.

visuals.label: After
visuals.caption: After: the same cart shows it's only $12.50 away from free shipping.
